# Code generator

Most of the SDK beyond the resources the official Node.js and Python SDKs
cover is generated from Bachs's OpenAPI spec by `gen.js`, a port of
`bachs-sdk-go/tools/gen/gen.js`. Generated files live in `lib/src/generated/`
and start with:

```
// Code generated by tool/gen/gen.js from tool/gen/openapi.json; DO NOT EDIT.
```

Don't edit those files. Change the generator or its config and run it again.
Every other file in `lib/src` is hand-written. The generator never touches
those, and reuses their types (`Product`, `Payment`, `Customer` and so on)
instead of generating duplicates.

## Regenerate

From the repository root (needs Node.js):

```sh
node tool/gen/gen.js tool/gen/openapi.json lib/src
dart format lib
dart analyze && dart test
```

Running it twice on the same spec produces identical files. It also rewrites
the `part` lines between `// BEGIN GENERATED PARTS` and
`// END GENERATED PARTS` in `lib/src/bachs.dart`.

## How generated code joins hand-written code

- A service with no hand-written class (such as `RefundsService`) is
  generated as a whole class. Add it to `BachsClient` in `client.dart`; the
  generator prints the list of such services.
- A service with a hand-written class (such as `PaymentsService`) gets its
  generated methods in a private mixin, `_PaymentsServiceGen`. The
  hand-written class must say `with _PaymentsServiceGen` and declare
  `@override final BachsClient _c;`.
- A type used only in responses gets `fromJson` and `raw`. A type used only
  in requests gets a constructor and `toJson`. A type used in both gets all
  of them, with request-style (nullable) fields.

## Update to a newer Bachs API

`openapi.json` is a pinned copy of the spec, so changes to the API show up as
a diff in review:

```sh
curl -sL https://docs.bachs.io/docs/openapi/openapi.json -o tool/gen/openapi.json
git diff --stat tool/gen/openapi.json
```

Then regenerate as above. A new operation is not picked up automatically: add
it to the `OPS` table at the top of `gen.js` with the service and method name
it should have (Go-style names; the generator lower-cases the first letter):

```js
['createRefund', 'Refunds', 'Create'],
['listRefunds', 'Refunds', 'List', { listAll: 'offset' }],
```

Options on an entry:

| Option | Use |
|---|---|
| `listAll: 'offset'` or `'cursor'` | Also generate a `listAll` stream |
| `listAllName` | Name the stream something other than `listAll` |
| `query` | Name for the query-parameter class |
| `body`, `resp` | Names for request and response types the spec defines inline |
| `noBody` | Send no body even if the spec allows an empty one |

Spec schemas that should map onto a hand-written type go in `EXISTING`, and
renamed types go in `RENAME`. Request bodies the spec leaves untyped are
described by hand in `MANUAL_SCHEMAS`. If generated code needs `fromJson` or
`toJson` on a hand-written type that lacks it, the generator stops and names
the type; add the method and list it in `HANDWRITTEN_CAN`.

Keep `OPS`, `EXISTING`, `RENAME` and `MANUAL_SCHEMAS` in step with the Go
SDK's generator so the two SDKs cover the same operations under the same
names.
